_instructions: This file is a TEMPLATE and authorizes nothing.  Its status field is not
AUTHORIZED and aws_supervisor_r3.validate_authorization_record refuses it;
preflight_r3.py P9 executes that refusal as a required control.
To authorize: (1) obtain a different-model hostile source PASS of this
packet and record its report path, SHA-256 and model in reviewer_pass,
with verdict spelled exactly PASS -- no other spelling, case or spacing
is accepted, and any model name that normalises to contain 'opus' is
refused as the producer;  (2) obtain the coordinator GO; (3) fill every
<...> sentinel with the live host's exact values; (4) set status to
AUTHORIZED; (5) freeze the file root-owned 0444; (6) set the live EC2 tag
jc2-d43-k0-field-cert-authorization-sha256 to this file's SHA-256.
The preregistration status is never edited.
One authorization authorizes at most one launch, ever, and R3 enforces
that on both sides of the privilege boundary.  ROOT, via the unit's
ExecStartPre=+ mint_claim_r3.sh, mints at most one claim per digest:
<sealed parent>/spent/<digest>.spent is created with O_EXCL before
anything else exists, so a unit restart dies at MINT_ALREADY_SPENT.  The
UNPRIVILEGED supervisor then takes at most one consumption lease,
<run_path>/.jc2-k0-r3-authorization-<digest>.lease, inside the
service-owned run directory, last, after every precondition has passed,
so a failed precondition never consumes this record.  A crashed or
NO_VERDICT run retires this record; a retry needs a new record, a new
digest and a new live tag.
DEPLOYMENT ORDER, which is not optional:
a. root creates the sealed parent <run_path>'s parent directory,
root-owned, mode 0755, symlink-free, with no group- or
world-writable ancestor;
b. root freezes THIS file 0444 root-owned and sets the live tag;
c. root runs mint_claim_r3.sh <sealed parent> <run name> <this file>
jc2k0 -- normally as the unit's ExecStartPre=+, which is the
supported path;
d. ops runs, AS jc2k0, custody_selftest_r3.py --on-host-dry-run
--run-path <run_path> --authorization <this file>.  It consumes
nothing and its JSON belongs in the coordinator record's notes;
e. only then start the unit.
run_path names a directory that root has ALREADY created for this exact
authorization: it must exist, be owned by jc2k0 with mode exactly 0700,
and hold the root-owned 0444 claim token and nothing else.  The
supervisor creates no directory anywhere.

run_path_note: root-minted, owned by jc2k0, mode exactly 0700, inside a root-owned non-group/world-writable sealed parent, holding only the root-owned 0444 claim token .jc2-k0-r3-claim-<digest>.json.  The supervisor verifies all of that and creates nothing; see README, 'The R3 privilege boundary'.
